main_text.head: SECTIO IV. DE OSSIBVS DORSI.
main_text.p: Quarta sectioPosteriora medii trunci ossa sunt ossa Dorsi.
DorsumDorsum dicitur id, quod à basi occipitis ad ipsum pertingit anum.
Eius ossaDorsi ossa sunt vertebrata, quae vertebris constant.
VertebraeVertebrae seu spondyli sunt ossa dorsi in crassiores nodos conglobata, in medio cava, spinalem medullam continentia.
Vertebrae partes sunt corpus ipsum & processus.
Corpus est ipsa pars quasi corpulenta vertebrae.
Processus est ea pars, quae in corpore quolibet loco protuberat.
Intra utrumq; est foramen dorsali medullae tuendae paratum.

Os totum vertebratum generaliter dicitur Spina dorsiSpina dorsi: quae est os posterius trunci medii viginti quatuor varie invicem articulatis constans vertebris, ad motū flexionis & erectionis appositum.
Ossa seu spina dorsi est superior vel In-ferior.

page.notes: The side note "Quarta sectio" stands beside the division heading and is placed at the start of the first paragraph. Faint grey text in the left margin (near "Tertia sectio" and "Ossa pe... dorsi") and faint mirrored text across the text block are show-through from the other side of the leaf and are not transcribed. The "Spina dorsi" note sits beside the line "ditur Spina dorsi" and is placed at that point. The "Sectio" mark and faint letters at the foot are show-through or a signature that could not be read reliably, and are omitted. The word "Ossa" in "Ossa seu spina dorsi" is set in italic and read with some uncertainty; the printed line is "Ossa seu spina dorsi est superior vel In-ferior."
